_comment: Hand-curated gear catalog for the studio builder. Prices are approximate USD street prices - review quarterly (see docs/studio-builder-plan.md). 'search' terms feed the merchant URL builder in src/lib/affiliate.ts.

items.name: Audio-Technica ATH-M20x
items.why: The cheapest headphones that are honest enough to make production decisions on.

items.name: AKG K240 Studio
items.why: Semi-open classic with a wide, natural sound for mixing - not for loud rooms or DJ booths.

items.name: Sony MDR-7506
items.why: The studio workhorse for four decades - flat, revealing, and folds up for the backpack.

items.name: Sennheiser HD 25
items.why: The DJ-booth standard: loud, isolating, one-ear monitoring, and survives being sat on.

items.name: Audio-Technica ATH-M50x
items.why: Do-everything closed-back: punchy enough for DJing, accurate enough for production.

items.name: Beyerdynamic DT 770 Pro (80 Ohm)
items.why: Supremely comfortable closed-back with deep bass extension - great for long sessions and tracking.

items.name: Sennheiser HD 600
items.why: Open-back mixing reference - the midrange truth-teller mixes get checked on.

items.name: PreSonus Eris 3.5 (pair)
items.why: Tiny desk monitors that beat any computer speakers - the honest entry point.

items.name: IK Multimedia iLoud Micro Monitor (pair)
items.why: Astonishing accuracy from speakers the size of a coffee mug - the small-room specialist.

items.name: JBL 305P MkII (pair)
items.why: Wide sweet spot and serious low end for the money - the default first 'real' monitors.

items.name: Kali Audio LP-6 (pair)
items.why: Punches at twice its price with boundary EQ for untreated rooms.

items.name: Yamaha HS5 (pair)
items.why: Descendant of the NS-10: ruthless midrange honesty that translates everywhere.

items.name: ADAM Audio T7V (pair)
items.why: Ribbon-tweeter detail and real low-end reach for a serious step-up room.

items.name: Behringer U-Phoria UMC22
items.why: The functional minimum: one decent preamp, clean output, absurdly cheap.

items.name: Focusrite Scarlett Solo (4th Gen)
items.why: The best-selling interface ever for a reason: great preamp, idiot-proof, works everywhere.

items.name: MOTU M2
items.why: Best converters and metering in its class - the pick if the interface is the studio's heart.

items.name: Audient iD14 MkII
items.why: Console-grade preamps and a proper monitor controller in a desktop box.

items.name: Numark Party Mix II
items.why: A real two-channel controller with pads and a built-in soundcard for pocket money.

items.name: Hercules DJControl Inpulse 300 MK2
items.why: Bigger jog wheels and beatmatch training guides - the learning-focused step up.

items.name: Pioneer DJ DDJ-FLX4
items.why: The default first controller: rekordbox and Serato support, club-style layout, endless tutorials.

items.name: Pioneer DJ DDJ-FLX6-GT
items.why: Four channels, full-size jogs, and merge FX - the last controller before club gear.

items.name: Pioneer DJ DDJ-FLX10
items.why: Flagship 4-channel with stems separation - for DJs booking real gigs.

items.name: Arturia MiniLab 3
items.why: Best-feeling mini keys and a serious bundled software suite (Analog Lab).

items.name: Akai MPK Mini MK3
items.why: The beatmaker classic: MPC pads plus two octaves of keys in a backpack footprint.

items.name: Novation Launchkey 37 MK4
items.why: Full-size keys with deep Ableton integration and a proper arpeggiator.

items.name: Shure SM58
items.why: Indestructible dynamic that forgives untreated rooms - the safe first vocal mic.

items.name: Audio-Technica AT2020
items.why: The classic budget condenser: detailed vocals if the room is reasonably quiet.

items.name: RODE NT1 (5th Gen)
items.why: Near-silent self-noise and 32-bit float USB output - a condenser to grow into.
